stories.title_en: Swapping a Fake Ingot for Real Silver

paragraphs.zh: 泉州府客人孫滔，為人誠實，有長者風。帶銀百餘兩，往南京買布。在沿山搭船，陡遇一棍名汪蘭，詐稱興化府人，鄉語略同，因與孫同船數日，甚歡。習知滔樸實人，的可騙也。因言他故，往蕪湖起岸買貨。舟中說他尚未傾銀，有銀一錠，細絲，十二兩重，若有便銀，打換為妙，意在就孫換之。孫因請看，汪欣然取出真銀。孫接過手，曰：「果是金花細絲。」汪欲顯真銀，因轉在孫手接出，遍與舟中客人看，問：「好否？」都道：「是細絲。」遂因舟上有筆硯在，汪微微冷笑，將此銀寫「十二兩足在風窠底」。孫心中道：「此人輕薄，有銀何必如此翻弄？」因潛對汪曰：「出來人，謹慎些。」汪曰：「無妨。」孫因問：「要換折多少？」汪曰：「弟只零買雜貨，憑兄銀色估折便是。」孫因取出小八九錢重的，只九一二成色。汪看喜曰：「此銀九四五傾來麼？俱一樣如此即好矣。」蓋汪重估孫銀水，使孫樂換。孫取天平兩對，估折明白。汪即箱中取出白綿紙，與孫麵包作兩包。汪因佯起，轉身一回，故意誤收原銀入袖，曰：「此包是我的了。」孫曰：「不是，這包是你的。」汪即替出那假，亦綿紙包，與真銀一樣，交與孫收。孫接過手，亦微開包緊，見銀字無異，概不深省，即鎖封笥篋中。汪須臾起岸分別。孫一向到南京，取出前銀，乃是錫，懊恨無及，始知被他替包騙去矣。
paragraphs.en: A traveler from Quanzhou Prefecture, Sun Tao, was honest, with the manner of an elder. He carried more than a hundred taels of silver to Nanjing to buy cloth. He boarded a boat along the mountains and suddenly met a swindler named Wang Lan, who pretended to be from Xinghua Prefecture, with a roughly similar dialect. He was on the same boat with Sun for several days and they were quite happy. He learned that Tao was a simple, honest man, truly swindleable. On some pretext he said he would go ashore at Wuhu to buy goods. On the boat he said he had not yet melted his silver; he had one ingot, fine-thread, twelve taels, and if there was convenient silver, exchanging would be best—his intent was to exchange with Sun. Sun asked to see it; Wang gladly took out real silver. Sun took it and said, "It truly is jinhua fine-thread." Wang, wanting to show it was real silver, took it back from Sun's hand, showed it all around to the boat passengers, and asked, "Is it good?" All said, "It's fine-thread." Then, because there were brush and inkstone on the boat, Wang gave a faint cold smile and wrote on this silver "twelve taels full, at the wind-nest bottom." Sun thought, "This man is frivolous; if you have silver, why fuss with it like this?" He quietly told Wang, "When traveling, be more careful." Wang said, "No harm." Sun then asked, "How much discount for the exchange?" Wang said, "I only buy miscellaneous goods in small amounts; I'll go by whatever purity you estimate, brother." Sun then took out small pieces of eight or nine qian, only 91–92 percent purity. Wang looked and said gladly, "Was this silver poured at 94–95? If all of it is like this, that's fine." For Wang overestimated Sun's silver quality, to make Sun happy to exchange. Sun took a balance and they matched both sides, the estimate clear. Wang then took white cotton paper from his chest and with Sun wrapped it into two parcels. Wang then pretended to get up, turned around, and deliberately by mistake put the original silver into his sleeve, saying, "This parcel is mine now." Sun said, "No, this parcel is yours." Wang then substituted the fake, also wrapped in cotton paper, looking the same as the real silver, and handed it to Sun. Sun took it, slightly opened the tight parcel, saw the writing on the silver was no different, did not look deeply, and locked it in his chest. In a moment Wang went ashore and they parted. Sun went on to Nanjing, took out the earlier silver—it was tin. Regret was too late; only then did he know he had been swapped-and-swindled.

paragraphs.zh: 按：孫滔，樸實人也。其看銀時，但稱彼輕薄，不知此人輕薄處，正要如此，人方不疑，後方好用假。不然，待打換之後，或有人從旁取視，豈不敗機？故坐舟冷笑，為書銀模樣，無非為眩視計耳，向後誰復細認哉？說者曰：「假令包銀時，孫即取真銀入手，後令汪取銀，則汪不窮乎？」曰：「雖然，彼棍者變計百端，即令真銀入手，彼又別有脫法。」但各守本分，各用己財，勿貪小可便宜，則不落圈套矣。
paragraphs.en: Note: Sun Tao was a simple, honest man. When looking at the silver, he only called the other frivolous, not knowing that this man's frivolity was exactly what was needed, so people would not suspect, and later the fake could be used. Otherwise, after the exchange, if someone from the side took it to look, would the scheme not fail? So sitting on the boat with a cold smile, writing on the silver's surface, was all a plan to dazzle the eyes; afterward who would look closely again? Some say: "Suppose when wrapping the silver, Sun had taken the real silver into his own hand, then let Wang take silver—wouldn't Wang be at a loss?" Answer: "Even so, that swindler has a hundred changing plans; even if the real silver were in hand, he would have another way to strip it." Just each keep to his own lot, each use his own money, don't greed for a small advantage, and you will not fall into the trap.

paragraphs.zh: 賁監生在南監，期滿將歸，欲換好金數十兩，歸遺妻妾，以將遠敬。同鄉鄧監生阻之曰：「京城換金者，屢被棍以銅脫去。金非急用，何必在此換為？」賁曰：「京城方有好金。若有棍能脫我者，亦服他好手段。」數日內換金十餘兩，皆照金色交易，都是好金。
paragraphs.en: Jiansheng Ben was in the Southern Imperial Academy; his term was up and he was about to return. He wanted to exchange several dozen taels of good gold to take home as a gift for his wives and concubines, as a distant token of respect. Fellow-townsman Jiansheng Deng stopped him: "Those who exchange gold in the capital have often been stripped by swindlers using copper. Gold is not urgently needed—why exchange it here?" Ben said, "Only the capital has good gold. If some swindler can strip me, I'll admire his skill." Within a few days he exchanged more than ten taels of gold, all traded according to gold quality, all good gold.

paragraphs.zh: 後有一後生，以金錠十二兩來換。賁生取看，幾有足色金。問其換數，後生曰：「某鄉官命換的，要作五換。」賁遞與鄧看，曰：「此金可有六換，若五換，價公道矣。」鄧看曰：「果好。可將此金對明收起，勿過他手，然後對銀六十兩還之。」賁依言，先收入此金，然後還其銀。後生不得展轉，只得領銀歸，見其父，云：「兩監生如此關妨，不能再脫出。」父頓足曰：「一家生意在此，把本子送去了，何以為生？速去訪此監生何時歸？」回報：「已討定船，某日刻期登舟矣。」體探已的。
paragraphs.en: Later a young man came to exchange a twelve-tael gold ingot. Ben took it to look; it was nearly full-purity gold. He asked the exchange rate. The young man said, "A certain country gentleman ordered it exchanged, at five-for-one." Ben passed it to Deng to look: "This gold could go at six-for-one; at five, the price is fair." Deng looked and said, "Truly good. You can match this gold clearly and put it away, don't let it pass through his hands again, then pay him sixty taels of silver." Ben followed the advice, first took in this gold, then paid the silver. The young man could not work a switch, had to take the silver home, and told his father: "The two jiansheng were so cautious; I couldn't strip it again." The father stamped his feet: "The family's livelihood is in this; we've sent the capital away—how will we live? Quickly find out when this jiansheng goes home." Report came back: "They've already booked a boat, departing on a certain day at a set time." The reconnaissance was confirmed.

paragraphs.zh: 至期，兩監生到船坐定。老棍裝為一道士，衣冠淨潔，亦來搭船，舵工收之在船中。共談處，道士言詞雍容，或談及京中官民事體，一一練熟。兩監生及同船諸人，亦樂與談。兩日後，將近晚間，道士故提及辨珠玉寶貝之法，諸人閒談一番。又說到辨金上去，道他更辨得真。賁監生因自誇彼在京換一錠足色金，換數又便宜。諸人中有求看估色數者，賁生誇耀，取出與諸人遞觀，皆誇羨好金。遍觀已訖，時天色漸晚，复付還賁生。將收入箱際，道士亦曰：「願藉觀。」接過一看，曰：「果好真金！」隨手即付還訖，又道及別新話上去。賁監生收入金。晚飯已熟，各散而餐。飲日，道士以船錢還舵工，與諸人別而登岸去。
paragraphs.en: On the day, the two jiansheng sat down on the boat. The old swindler dressed as a Daoist, clothes and cap clean, also came to take the boat; the helmsman took him aboard. In conversation the Daoist's speech was elegant; when talk turned to official and civilian affairs in the capital, he knew them all thoroughly. The two jiansheng and others on the boat were glad to talk with him. After two days, near evening, the Daoist deliberately brought up methods of distinguishing pearls, jade, and treasures; everyone chatted a while. Then they came to distinguishing gold; he said he could tell it even more truly. Jiansheng Ben then boasted that in the capital he had exchanged one ingot of full-purity gold, and the rate was cheap besides. Among the people some asked to look and estimate the quality. Ben, showing off, took it out and passed it around; all praised the good gold. After everyone had looked, the sky was gradually darkening; it was given back to Ben. Just as he was about to put it in the chest, the Daoist also said, "May I have a look?" He took it, looked once: "Truly good real gold!" Then immediately handed it back, and went on to other new talk. Jiansheng Ben put the gold away. Dinner was ready; they scattered to eat. The next day the Daoist paid the boat fare to the helmsman, took leave of everyone, and went ashore.

paragraphs.zh: 及賁監生歸，以金分贈妻妾。數日後，叫匠人來打釧鈿。先以小錠金打，匠皆稱金好。賁誇曰：「更換有一錠十二兩的尤好。」匠曰：「大錠金京中光棍多以銅脫人。」賁曰：「取與你看，有何棍能脫我乎？」匠接過手，笑曰：「正是銅也。」賁怪之，急取回看曰：「果銅也。我與鄧相公看定是上好金，又同船諸人看皆是好金，何都被瞞過？」忽猛省曰：「噯，是也！最後是一道士看，付還時天色近晚，我未及再檢視，即收藏箱中。是此時換去也！此道士何得一銅如此相似，又早已在手，如此換得容易？想京中換金後生，即老棍之子，彼換時未能脫，故來搭船脫歸也。」
paragraphs.en: When Jiansheng Ben got home, he divided the gold as gifts for wives and concubines. After several days he called a craftsman to make bracelets and hairpins. First he had small ingots made; the craftsmen all said the gold was good. Ben boasted: "I also exchanged a twelve-tael ingot that's even better." The craftsman said, "In the capital, swindlers often strip people with copper in large gold ingots." Ben said, "Take a look—what swindler could strip me?" The craftsman took it and laughed: "This is copper." Ben was startled, quickly took it back: "It really is copper. Deng and I looked and it was first-rate gold, and everyone on the boat said it was good gold—how were we all fooled?" Suddenly he realized: "Ah, that's it! Last to look was a Daoist; when he handed it back the sky was nearly dark; I didn't inspect again and put it in the chest. That's when it was swapped! How could this Daoist have copper so similar, already in hand, and swap so easily? I think the young man who exchanged gold in the capital was the old swindler's son; he couldn't strip it at the exchange, so he came on the boat to strip it on the way home."

paragraphs.zh: 按：老棍之脫賁生金也，人謂其棍真高手矣。吾曰不然。設若賁生韜藏不露，則老棍雖有諸葛神機，莊周妙智，安能得其金而窺之？何以脫為？故責在賁生矜誇炫耀，是自招其脫也。噫！
paragraphs.en: Note: As for the old swindler stripping Jiansheng Ben's gold, people say this swindler is truly a high hand. I say otherwise. If Ben had kept it hidden and not shown it, then even if the old swindler had Zhuge Liang's divine schemes and Zhuang Zhou's subtle wisdom, how could he get the gold and look at it? How could he strip it? So the blame is on Ben's boasting and showing off; he invited the stripping himself. Alas!
